title: Model Discrimination & Calibration Atlas — What Would Make One Explanation Better Than Another?
purpose: Move project testing beyond 'can mathematics be attached?' toward discriminating predictions, calibration, uncertainty, negative controls, competing models and explicit failure conditions.

claim_ladder.question: Is the object/relationship described clearly and reproducibly?
Is there a measured pattern beyond anecdotal selection?
Is there a formal mechanism producing observables?
Can parameters be estimated from declared data without arbitrary tuning?
Does the model predict something meaningfully different from plausible alternatives?
Does performance survive new samples, contexts or independent reproduction?
Do interventions, natural experiments or mechanism-specific evidence support the proposed causal story?

required: prediction made before evaluation where possible
negative control or placebo where meaningful
out-of-sample or holdout strategy where meaningful

model_comparison.rule: Always ask what a simple null/baseline explains before invoking a richer project model.
Compare against at least one plausible non-project explanation, not only random noise.
A more flexible model must earn its extra parameters through predictive or explanatory gain.
Inspect where the model fails, not only fit summary.
Vary reasonable preprocessing, thresholds and priors to see whether conclusions are fragile.
State the population/domain to which the test applies before generalizing elsewhere.

uncertainty_types.meaning: Uncertainty because available cases are a subset of a larger population.
Range of model parameter values compatible with data.
Uncertainty about the model form itself.
Multiple meanings can fit the same factual pattern.

negative_controls: Randomize or permute labels/links when appropriate to test whether a pattern survives arbitrary structure.
Use non-matching time windows or comparison groups where domain logic permits.
Fit alternative geometries to a claimed spiral/shape rather than judging visual resemblance.
Compare derivative versus independent sources when measuring corroboration.
Test whether a symbolic mapping still seems unique after generating plausible alternative mappings.
promotion_rules: A formal equation without measurable variables remains conceptual/formal, not empirically validated.
A good in-sample fit without comparison or holdout is insufficient for strong promotion.
A single successful prediction does not validate unrelated metaphysical claims attached to the same symbol.
Failure should downgrade or narrow the claim rather than being reinterpreted automatically as confirmation.
Replicable null results belong in the archive because they constrain future theory.
